questions.s: In which year was the War of Independence (the Revolt) against the East India Company fought?
questions.e: The great revolt against Company rule broke out in 1857, beginning at Meerut and spreading to Delhi. 1875 is the year the MAO College was founded at Aligarh, a different event.

questions.s: Who was the last Mughal emperor, exiled to Rangoon after 1857?
questions.e: Bahadur Shah Zafar, a poet as well as a ruler, was tried by the British and exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862. Aurangzeb died in 1707, long before the revolt.

questions.s: Who founded the Aligarh Movement to promote modern education among the Muslims of India?
questions.e: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan led the Aligarh Movement and founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875. Iqbal was a poet-philosopher of a later generation.

questions.s: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was founded in
questions.e: Sir Syed opened the MAO College in 1875; it later became Aligarh Muslim University. 1885 is the year of the Indian National Congress and 1906 of the Muslim League.

questions.s: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote a pamphlet on the causes of the 1857 revolt. What is it called?
questions.e: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (1859) argued that the revolt came from British policy mistakes and not from Muslims alone. Asar-us-Sanadid is his work on the monuments of Delhi, and Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was his journal.

questions.s: The Scientific Society set up by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan aimed to
o: publish a daily newspaper in English
questions.e: Sir Syed set up the society so that modern learning could reach Muslims in their own language, through Urdu translations of Western works.

questions.s: The Indian National Congress was founded in
questions.e: The Congress was formed in December 1885, with A. O. Hume playing a key part. The All-India Muslim League followed in 1906, and the Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916.

questions.s: Which retired British official is credited with helping found the Indian National Congress?
questions.e: Allan Octavian Hume helped to organise the first Congress session in 1885. Curzon and Minto were Viceroys, and Radcliffe chaired the 1947 boundary commissions.

questions.s: The Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867 began in which city?
questions.e: The demand to replace Urdu in the Persian script by Hindi in courts began in Banaras in 1867. It made Sir Syed fear for the cultural future of Muslims, though Lahore became a later centre of the debate.

questions.s: The Partition of Bengal took place in
questions.e: Lord Curzon divided Bengal in 1905, creating a Muslim-majority eastern province with Dhaka as capital. It was annulled in 1911, and 1935 is the year of a major Act.

questions.s: Which Viceroy carried out the Partition of Bengal?
questions.e: Lord Curzon (Viceroy 1899–1905) partitioned Bengal for administrative reasons. Minto received the Simla Deputation in 1906, and Wavell and Linlithgow served in the 1930s and 1940s.

questions.s: The partition of Bengal was annulled in
questions.e: After strong Hindu protest and the Swadeshi movement, the British cancelled the partition in 1911, which disappointed many Muslims. 1909 is the year of the Morley-Minto reforms.

questions.s: The Simla Deputation of 1906 met which Viceroy?
questions.e: In October 1906 a Muslim delegation led by Sir Aga Khan III met Lord Minto in Simla to ask for separate electorates. Mountbatten was the last Viceroy, in 1947.

questions.s: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906?
questions.e: The deputation was led by Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, Aga Khan III. Sir Syed had died in 1898, and Jinnah had not yet joined the Muslim League.

questions.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded in
questions.e: It was founded on 30 December 1906 during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. 1885 is the year of the Congress and 1940 of the Lahore Resolution.

questions.s: In which city was the All-India Muslim League founded?
questions.e: The League was founded at Dhaka, in a meeting hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan. Karachi is the city of Jinnah's birth, not the League's.

questions.s: Who became the first permanent president of the All-India Muslim League?
questions.e: Sir Aga Khan III was its first permanent (honorary) president. Nawab Salimullah hosted the 1906 meeting and proposed the party, but was not its president.

questions.s: Which feature of the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 was the main gain for Muslims?
questions.e: The 1909 reforms accepted separate electorates for Muslims in the legislative councils. Dyarchy came in 1919 and provincial autonomy in 1935.

questions.s: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the
questions.e: The Montagu-Chelmsford reforms of 1919 split provincial subjects into transferred and reserved. The 1935 Act replaced dyarchy with provincial autonomy.

questions.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between
o: the Muslim League and the Crown
questions.e: At Lucknow the two parties agreed on a joint reform scheme, and the Congress accepted separate electorates. Jinnah played a leading role.

questions.s: Which leader is known as the architect of the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
questions.e: Jinnah, a member of both parties then, helped to bring them together, which earned him a reputation as an ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity. Rahmat Ali is linked to the name Pakistan.

questions.s: The Khilafat Movement of India aimed to protect the position of the
questions.e: Indian Muslims supported the Ottoman Caliph after the First World War, fearing his removal. The Mughal throne had already ended in 1857.

questions.s: Which brothers were leaders of the Khilafat Movement?
questions.e: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were known as the Ali Brothers. Sikandar Hayat and Fazlul Huq were provincial leaders, not brothers.

questions.s: The Khilafat Movement lost its basis when which country abolished the caliphate in 1924?
questions.e: Turkey, under Mustafa Kemal, abolished the caliphate in 1924, leaving the movement without a cause. Egypt and Iraq were not the seat of the Ottoman Caliph.

questions.s: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it
o: banned the use of Urdu in courts
questions.e: The Rowlatt Act gave the government power to detain suspects without a trial, which Indians saw as unjust. It had no direct link to language or electorates.

questions.s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in which city in 1919?
questions.e: On 13 April 1919 British troops fired on a peaceful crowd at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar. Meerut is where the revolt of 1857 began.

questions.s: The Hijrat Movement of 1920 involved Muslims migrating from India to
questions.e: Thousands of Indian Muslims, regarding British India as hostile territory, moved towards Afghanistan; the movement ended in hardship. Turkey was the seat of the Caliph but was not the destination.

questions.s: The Simon Commission was boycotted in India mainly because it
questions.e: The 1927 commission under Sir John Simon consisted only of British members, which angered Indians of all parties. Its proposals did not offer independence.

questions.s: Who produced the Nehru Report of 1928?
questions.e: Motilal Nehru chaired the committee that drafted the report. Jawaharlal was his son and a secretary of the committee. The report rejected separate electorates, so Muslims opposed it.

questions.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were announced in
questions.e: Jinnah put the Fourteen Points before the Muslim League in March 1929 as the reply to the Nehru Report. 1940 is the year of the Lahore Resolution.

questions.s: Which demand was part of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
questions.e: The Fourteen Points asked that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency and reforms be introduced in the NWFP and Balochistan. The Punjab partition was not a demand.

questions.s: Allama Iqbal gave his famous presidential address at which Muslim League session?
questions.e: Iqbal spoke at Allahabad in December 1930, and the address outlined a state for Muslims in the north-west of India. Lahore was where the 1940 resolution was passed.

questions.s: The Allahabad Address of Allama Iqbal was delivered in
questions.e: Iqbal's address came on 29 December 1930 and is seen as the first clear public expression of the idea of a Muslim homeland. In 1940, Jinnah presided at Lahore.

questions.s: In his Allahabad Address, Iqbal proposed a Muslim state consisting of Punjab, NWFP, Sindh and
questions.e: Iqbal proposed uniting these north-western provinces, with Balochistan, into a single state within India. Bengal was not part of his proposal.

questions.s: In which city was Allama Iqbal born?
questions.e: Iqbal was born in Sialkot in 1877 and died in Lahore in 1938. Aligarh was the centre of Sir Syed's work.

questions.s: Which of these works of Iqbal was written in Persian?
questions.e: Asrar-e-Khudi (1915) is a Persian masnavi. The other three are mainly Urdu collections, though Iqbal also wrote much in Persian.

questions.s: The name 'Pakistan' was first put forward in 1933 by
questions.e: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, a student at Cambridge, coined the name in his pamphlet 'Now or Never'. Iqbal described a state but did not use the name.

questions.s: In the name 'Pakistan' as coined by Rahmat Ali, the letter 'S' stands for
questions.e: Rahmat Ali built the name from P for Punjab, A for Afghania (NWFP), K for Kashmir, S for Sindh and 'tan' for Balochistan. The others are towns or regions that are not part of the formula.

questions.s: Rahmat Ali's pamphlet of 1933 was titled
questions.e: The pamphlet 'Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish for Ever?' appealed for a separate Muslim state. The other three titles are not real works of his.

questions.s: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced which system in the provinces?
questions.e: The 1935 Act gave elected ministries real power in the provinces and ended dyarchy. Presidential rule was not part of the colonial scheme.

questions.s: Provincial elections under the Government of India Act 1935 were held in
questions.e: The first elections under the new Act took place in the winter of 1936–37. The 1946 elections came after the Second World War.

questions.s: Which party won the largest share of seats in the 1937 elections and formed ministries in most provinces?
questions.e: The Congress won a majority in most provinces and formed ministries in several, while the League did poorly. The Unionist Party was strong only in the Punjab.

questions.s: The Congress ministries of 1937–39 resigned in protest against
o: the passing of the Lahore Resolution
the annulment of the Bengal partition
the proposals of the Simon Commission
India's entry into the Second World War
questions.e: They resigned in 1939 because India was brought into the war without consulting elected leaders. The Lahore Resolution came later, in 1940.

questions.s: The Muslim League observed which day after the Congress ministries resigned in 1939?
questions.e: On 22 December 1939 Muslims celebrated release from Congress rule, which Jinnah termed a Day of Deliverance. Direct Action Day came in 1946.

questions.s: The Lahore Resolution was passed in
questions.e: It was passed on 23 March 1940 during the League session held at Lahore. 1930 was the year of the Allahabad Address.

questions.s: On which date is Pakistan Day observed?
questions.e: Pakistan Day marks the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940. 14 August is Independence Day, 25 December Jinnah's birthday and 9 November Iqbal's.

questions.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of 1940?
questions.e: Jinnah gave the presidential address and set out the two-nation theory. Iqbal had died in 1938, two years before.

questions.s: Who moved the Lahore Resolution in 1940?
questions.e: The resolution was moved by Fazlul Huq, then Chief Minister of Bengal, and seconded by Khaliquzzaman. Sikandar Hayat was Premier of the Punjab.

questions.s: Who seconded the Lahore Resolution on behalf of the United Provinces?
questions.e: Khaliquzzaman seconded the resolution on behalf of the Muslims of the United Provinces. Others spoke later in support, but he was the formal seconder.

questions.s: Minar-e-Pakistan stands in which Lahore park?
questions.e: The tower was built where the 1940 session was held, in a park then called Minto Park and now Iqbal Park. Shalimar Garden is a Mughal garden elsewhere in the city.

questions.s: The Lahore Resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped as
o: a part of the Congress state
questions.e: The resolution called for areas of Muslim majority to be grouped into independent states with autonomy. It did not seek a single province nor to join the Congress.

questions.s: The August Offer of 1940 was made by which Viceroy?
questions.e: Lord Linlithgow's offer promised an expansion of the Viceroy's Council and a constituent body after the war. Wavell succeeded him in 1943.

questions.s: The Cripps Mission came to India in
questions.e: Sir Stafford Cripps came in March 1942 during the war with a draft promising dominion status after it. The Cabinet Mission arrived in 1946.

questions.s: Which movement did Gandhi and the Congress launch in August 1942?
questions.e: The Congress called on the British to quit India in 1942, and its leaders were arrested. The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.

questions.s: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of 1944 were held in
questions.e: Gandhi and Jinnah met at Jinnah's house in Bombay in September 1944 but could not agree. The talks followed the Rajagopalachari formula.

questions.s: The Simla Conference of 1945 was called by which Viceroy?
questions.e: Lord Wavell invited leaders to discuss an Executive Council. It failed when Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League could name Muslim members.

questions.s: Why did the Simla Conference of 1945 fail?
o: The League demanded the right to name all Muslim members
The Congress walked out of the conference hall
The Viceroy resigned before the talks ended
The British government withdrew the proposed plan
questions.e: The League insisted on choosing all Muslim members of the Council, which the Congress and the Viceroy could not accept. The Viceroy did not resign.

questions.s: In the elections of 1945–46, the Muslim League won all the Muslim seats in the
questions.e: The League won every one of the thirty reserved Muslim seats in the Central Legislature, proving it spoke for Indian Muslims. It also won most Muslim provincial seats.

questions.s: The Cabinet Mission came to India in
questions.e: The mission of three British Cabinet ministers arrived in March 1946 to settle the future of India. The Cripps Mission was the one of 1942.

questions.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 proposed grouping provinces into
questions.e: The plan proposed a weak Centre and three groups of provinces. Group B was to hold the north-western Muslim provinces and Group C Bengal and Assam.

questions.s: Which of these was a member of the Cabinet Mission 1946?
questions.e: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander made up the Cabinet Mission. Mountbatten and Wavell were Viceroys, and Radcliffe chaired the boundary commissions.

questions.s: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on
questions.e: The League called for it in July 1946 after the Cabinet Mission plan broke down, and it was observed on 16 August 1946. Communal violence followed in Calcutta. 14 August 1947 is Independence Day.

questions.s: Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
questions.e: Mountbatten arrived in March 1947 and oversaw the transfer of power. Wavell was his predecessor.

questions.s: The Partition Plan of 3 June 1947 is also known as the
questions.e: Lord Mountbatten announced it on 3 June 1947 and it provided for two dominions, India and Pakistan. The Wavell Plan was the Simla scheme of 1945.

questions.s: The British Parliament passed the Independence Act for India and Pakistan in
questions.e: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent in July 1947 and took effect on 15 August in India and 14 August in Pakistan. 1946 was the Cabinet Mission year.

questions.s: The Boundary Commissions of 1947 were headed by
questions.e: Radcliffe chaired the commissions for Punjab and Bengal, and his award was announced on 17 August. Cripps led the 1942 mission, and Simon the 1927 commission.

questions.s: When was the referendum that decided that the NWFP would join Pakistan?
questions.e: The people of the NWFP voted in July 1947, with a majority choosing Pakistan. A similar vote was held in the Sylhet district of Assam.

questions.s: Which date does Pakistan observe as its Independence Day?
questions.e: Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947, the 27th of Ramadan 1366 AH. India's independence day is 15 August. Jinnah died on 11 September 1948.

questions.s: Where and when was Quaid-e-Azam born?
questions.e: Jinnah was born in Karachi on 25 December 1876. The other options mix his birthplace or date with other occasions; Iqbal, not Jinnah, was born in Sialkot.

questions.s: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.e: Jinnah took the oath as Governor-General in Karachi on 15 August 1947. Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister.

questions.s: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.e: Liaquat Ali Khan held the office from 1947 until he was assassinated in 1951. Nazimuddin succeeded him.

questions.s: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah died in
questions.e: Jinnah died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi, little more than a year after independence. 1951 was the year Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated.

questions.s: In which city was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated in 1951?
questions.e: He was shot at a public meeting in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. The park, then Company Bagh, is now called Liaquat Bagh.

questions.s: Which title is given to Liaquat Ali Khan?
questions.e: Liaquat Ali Khan is called Quaid-e-Millat, 'Leader of the Nation'. Quaid-e-Azam is Jinnah's title and Madar-e-Millat is Fatima Jinnah's.

questions.s: Which title is given to Fatima Jinnah?
questions.e: Fatima Jinnah, sister of Quaid-e-Azam, is known as Madar-e-Millat, 'Mother of the Nation'. Quaid-e-Millat refers to Liaquat Ali Khan.

questions.s: Quaid-e-Azam delivered his famous address to the first Constituent Assembly on
questions.e: On 11 August 1947 Jinnah was elected president of the Constituent Assembly and gave a speech on equal rights for all citizens. 14 August was independence day itself.

questions.s: Shah Waliullah of Delhi is remembered chiefly as an
questions.e: Shah Waliullah (1703–1762) wrote on Islamic thought and called for reform and unity among Muslims. He was neither a soldier nor a colonial official.

questions.s: The Battle of Balakot of 1831 was fought between the followers of Syed Ahmad Shaheed and the
questions.e: Syed Ahmad Barelvi and Shah Ismail were killed by the Sikh army at Balakot. The British did not take part in this battle.

questions.s: Which battle of 1757 is seen as the start of British political power in Bengal?
questions.e: At Plassey Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daula, who was betrayed by Mir Jafar. Buxar (1764) later confirmed the Company's power, and Seringapatam (1799) ended Tipu Sultan.

questions.s: Which ruler of Mysore died fighting the British at Seringapatam in 1799?
questions.e: Tipu Sultan fell defending his capital. Hyder Ali was his father and died in 1782, while Siraj-ud-Daula was the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey.

questions.s: The Muhammadan Educational Conference, in whose session the Muslim League was founded, was established by
questions.e: Sir Syed founded the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886 to spread modern education. The League was born during its 1906 meeting at Dhaka.

questions.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by
questions.e: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced the Award, which kept separate electorates and extended them to other groups. The Poona Pact later modified the arrangement for the depressed classes.

questions.s: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed by Gandhi and
questions.e: The Poona Pact settled the representation of the depressed classes in the councils, replacing the separate electorate they had been granted. Jinnah was not a party.

questions.s: Gandhi ended the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 after violence at
questions.e: After a mob set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura, Gandhi called off the movement. Amritsar was the scene of the 1919 massacre.

questions.s: Which Muslim League leader of Bengal was known as 'Sher-e-Bangla'?
questions.e: A. K. Fazlul Huq was called Sher-e-Bangla, 'Tiger of Bengal', and moved the Lahore Resolution. Suhrawardy and Nazimuddin were Bengal leaders but are known by other titles.

questions.s: The Rajagopalachari Formula of 1944 was a proposal that
o: offered limited self-determination after the war
rejected any talks with Jinnah at all
questions.e: The formula, put forward by C. Rajagopalachari, offered the Muslim-majority areas a plebiscite after the war, but with conditions Jinnah found unsatisfactory. It did not ban the League.

questions.s: The Jinnah-Sikandar Pact of 1937 was concluded at
questions.e: At the Muslim League session at Lucknow in 1937, Sikandar Hayat Khan, Premier of the Punjab, agreed that Unionist Muslim members of the Punjab Assembly would also join the League party. Lahore was the 1940 venue.

questions.s: Jinnah returned to India from London to lead the Muslim League in
questions.e: Jinnah had been in England for several years before returning in 1934 and being elected League president. In 1913 he had first joined the League.

questions.s: In which year did Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Muslim League?
questions.e: Though already in the Congress, Jinnah joined the League in 1913. The League itself was founded in 1906.

questions.s: In the referendum of July 1947, which district of Assam voted to join Pakistan?
questions.e: Sylhet in the Muslim-majority east voted to join East Bengal, so it became part of Pakistan. The other places stayed with India.

questions.s: The provincial elections of 1937 were held while which Viceroy was in office?
questions.e: Linlithgow was Viceroy from 1936 to 1943, so the 1937 elections took place in his term. Wavell followed him, and Mountbatten came last in 1947.

questions.s: The Round Table Conferences in London were held between
questions.e: There were three conferences held in London in 1930–32 to discuss the future of India. Iqbal took part in the second and third meetings.

questions.s: The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was a resolution of which party?
questions.e: It was passed at the League's session in Lahore. At that time Jinnah led the League, and the Congress did not support it.

questions.s: Which day is observed in Pakistan as Iqbal Day?
questions.e: Iqbal was born on 9 November 1877. 25 December is the birthday of Jinnah.

questions.s: In which city is Quaid-e-Azam's mausoleum located?
questions.e: The Mazar-e-Quaid stands in Karachi, where Jinnah was born and died. Lahore holds the tomb of Allama Iqbal.

questions.s: Allama Iqbal is buried near which famous Lahore monument?
questions.e: Iqbal's tomb lies beside the steps of the Badshahi Mosque. Minar-e-Pakistan is a separate 20th-century memorial to the Lahore Resolution.

questions.s: The slogan of the Pakistan Movement meaning 'Pakistan means what?' ends with
questions.e: The popular slogan 'Pakistan ka matlab kya? La ilaha illallah' tied the demand for Pakistan to Islamic identity. The other phrases are not part of it.

questions.s: Which of these Acts first created provincial autonomy and proposed a federation for India?
questions.e: The 1935 Act proposed an All-India Federation, which was never fully set up, and gave autonomy to provinces. The 1919 Act had dyarchy instead.

questions.s: The Delhi Proposals of 1927 included acceptance of joint electorates in return for
questions.e: Muslim leaders offered to give up separate electorates if certain conditions, including a separate Sindh province, were met. The Congress did not fully accept them.

questions.s: Which Act of 1947 ended British rule and created two dominions?
questions.e: The Indian Independence Act 1947 created India and Pakistan as dominions. The Government of India Act 1935 was the earlier constitutional law.

questions.s: Who was the last Mughal emperor of India deported by the British after the revolt?
questions.e: Shah Jahan, Jahangir and Humayun ruled in earlier centuries. Only Bahadur Shah Zafar was deported to Burma after 1857.

questions.s: The 'Two-Nation Theory' states that Hindus and Muslims of India are
questions.e: The theory held that Muslims and Hindus differ in religion, culture and way of life and therefore form two nations. It does not describe one people.

questions.s: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly in
questions.e: The resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and adopted in March 1949. It set the guiding principles for later constitutions. 1956 is the year of the first constitution.

questions.s: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented it on 7 March and it was passed on 12 March 1949. Jinnah had died in September 1948.

questions.s: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to
questions.e: The Resolution states that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and that authority is exercised by the people as a sacred trust. It does not vest sovereignty in an Assembly or a ruler.

questions.s: Which law served as Pakistan's interim constitution from 1947, with adaptations?
questions.e: Pakistan adapted the 1935 Act as its working constitution until 1956. The 1919 Act was the earlier one with dyarchy.

questions.s: Pakistan's first constitution was enforced in
questions.e: It was adopted in February and enforced on 23 March 1956. The 1962 constitution was the second and the 1973 one the third.

questions.s: Under the 1956 Constitution, Pakistan became
questions.e: The 1956 Constitution declared the country an Islamic Republic, which is why 23 March is also remembered as Republic Day. Before that Pakistan was a Dominion.

questions.s: Who was the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
questions.e: Iskander Mirza was sworn in as President in March 1956. Ghulam Muhammad had been Governor-General before the post was replaced.

questions.s: The 1956 Constitution adopted which system of government?
questions.e: The 1956 Constitution gave a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister responsible to the National Assembly. The 1962 text was presidential.

questions.s: The principle of parity in the 1956 Constitution meant equal representation for
questions.e: Though East Pakistan had the larger population, the Constitution gave both wings equal seats in the legislature. This was a compromise, not a division by religion.

questions.s: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed by
questions.e: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the Constitution and declared martial law on 7 October 1958 and appointed Ayub Khan chief martial law administrator; Ayub removed Mirza shortly after. Bhutto came to office later.

questions.s: The One Unit scheme of 1955 merged
questions.e: One Unit combined the provinces and states of the western wing into the single province of West Pakistan, to match East Pakistan under parity. It was dissolved in 1970.

questions.s: The One Unit scheme was dissolved in
questions.e: West Pakistan was split into provinces again by Yahya Khan on 1 July 1970. 1973 is the year of the present constitution.

questions.s: The second constitution of Pakistan was enforced in
questions.e: Ayub Khan announced it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force in June 1962. It was abrogated in 1969.

questions.s: The 1962 Constitution introduced which system?
questions.e: Under the 1962 text real power lay with the President, who was both head of state and chief executive. A parliamentary system was used in 1956 and 1973.

questions.s: The 1962 Constitution used which indirect system for choosing the President?
questions.e: Voters elected Basic Democrats, 80,000 in all, and they formed the electoral college for the President and assemblies. Adult franchise was not used for the presidency.

questions.s: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in 1969 by
questions.e: Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969 and handed power to General Yahya Khan, who abrogated the Constitution and imposed martial law. Zia took over in 1977.

questions.s: The first general elections on the basis of adult franchise in Pakistan were held in
questions.e: They took place on 7 December 1970 for the National Assembly and the provincial assemblies. Earlier elections used limited franchise or indirect voting.

questions.s: East Pakistan became Bangladesh in
questions.e: East Pakistan separated after the war of 1971 and Bangladesh emerged on 16 December 1971. The 1973 date belongs to the constitution.

questions.s: The Constitution of 1973 was enforced on
questions.e: The National Assembly approved it on 10 April 1973 and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. 5 July 1977 is the date of Zia's martial law.

questions.s: Under whose leadership was the 1973 Constitution adopted?
questions.e: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto led the government that brought the Constitution. He was President when it was adopted and became Prime Minister when it took effect. Chaudhry Muhammad Ali led the 1956 text; Junejo served later.

questions.s: What is the system of government under the 1973 Constitution?
questions.e: Pakistan is a federation with a parliamentary form, where the Prime Minister heads the Cabinet. The 1962 version was presidential.

questions.s: The Parliament of Pakistan consists of the President, the National Assembly and the
questions.e: The Majlis-e-Shoora is bicameral, with a lower House and an upper House, the Senate. Courts are part of the judiciary, not the legislature.

questions.s: Which House represents the provinces equally?
questions.e: Every province has the same number of Senate seats, which protects smaller provinces. Seats in the National Assembly depend on population.

questions.s: In which House do money bills begin?
questions.e: Money bills must start in the National Assembly, which controls federal finance. The Senate can only make recommendations.

questions.s: What is the term of the National Assembly, unless dissolved earlier?
questions.e: The Assembly sits for five years from its first meeting. A six-year term is that of a Senator.

questions.s: What is the term of a member of the Senate?
questions.e: Senators serve six years, and half retire every three years. The National Assembly, not the Senate, has a five-year term.

questions.s: Who presides over the sittings of the National Assembly?
questions.e: The Speaker is elected by the members to preside over sittings. The Prime Minister is the head of government and answers to the House.

questions.s: Who is the head of state of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
questions.e: The President is the head of state and acts mostly on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister is chief executive.

questions.s: The President is elected by which group?
o: An electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies
questions.e: The members of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies form the college. People do not elect the President directly.

questions.s: What is the term of the President?
questions.e: The President holds office for five years. A Senator's term is six years and has no link to it.

questions.s: Who appoints the Governor of a province?
questions.e: The Governor is appointed by the President, usually on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Chief Minister heads the elected provincial government.

questions.s: Who heads the government of a province?
questions.e: The Chief Minister leads the provincial cabinet while the Governor is the federal representative. The Speaker presides over the assembly.

questions.s: The Federal Shariat Court was established to examine whether laws are
questions.e: It decides whether a law conflicts with the injunctions of Islam. It was set up in 1980, and its work differs from that of the Supreme Court.

questions.s: The Council of Islamic Ideology is a body that
o: advises on Islamic compatibility of laws
questions.e: The Council advises Parliament and the provinces on whether laws agree with Islamic teaching. It does not make laws, try cases or conduct elections.

questions.s: Under the Constitution, the national language of Pakistan is
questions.e: Article 251 declares Urdu as the national language. English is the official language until arrangements are made for Urdu.

questions.s: According to Article 2 of the Constitution, the state religion is
questions.e: Article 2 declares Islam as the State religion of Pakistan. Democracy and federalism are principles of government, not religions.

questions.s: The Constitution declares which of these as an official name of the country?
questions.e: Article 1 gives the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The 1962 Constitution had used only Republic of Pakistan at first.

questions.s: Which constitutional body conducts elections in Pakistan?
questions.e: The Election Commission, headed by the Chief Election Commissioner, organises elections. The Public Service Commission recruits civil servants.

questions.s: Which body is mainly responsible for distribution of federal revenues among the provinces?
questions.e: The NFC makes awards on sharing divisible tax revenue between the federation and provinces. The Council of Common Interests settles other inter-provincial issues.

questions.s: The Council of Common Interests is formed under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
questions.e: Article 153 sets up the Council to settle questions between the federation and the provinces. Article 251 deals with language and Article 8 with fundamental rights.

questions.s: Article 8 of the Constitution states that any law inconsistent with fundamental rights is
questions.e: Laws that take away fundamental rights are void to that extent. They do not need a vote of the Senate.

questions.s: High Courts have power to issue writs under which Article?
questions.e: Article 199 gives the High Courts writ jurisdiction. Article 184 relates to the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, and Article 6 to high treason.

questions.s: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with high treason?
questions.e: Article 6 makes abrogation or subversion of the Constitution high treason. Article 25 deals with equality of citizens.

questions.s: Which Amendment of 2010 reduced federal powers by abolishing the Concurrent List?
questions.e: The Eighteenth Amendment transferred many subjects to the provinces and renamed the NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Eighth belonged to the Zia era.

questions.s: What is the minimum age for a person to vote in elections in Pakistan?
questions.e: A citizen who is eighteen years old and registered on the roll may vote. 25 is the minimum age to stand for the National Assembly.

questions.s: What is the minimum age for a person to contest an election to the National Assembly?
questions.e: The National Assembly requires candidates to be at least 25. The Senate and the Presidency need higher ages.

questions.s: The minimum age for election as President is
questions.e: Article 41 sets the minimum age for President at 45. A person must also be a Muslim and qualified to be elected to the Assembly.

questions.s: Fundamental rights in the 1973 Constitution are listed in which Part?
questions.e: Part II, Chapter 1, lists the fundamental rights, and Chapter 2 sets out the Principles of Policy. Part I is introductory.

questions.s: A bill passed by one House and rejected by the other is resolved by
questions.e: When the Houses disagree, a joint sitting under Article 70 decides by a majority of the members present. Courts and referenda do not decide.

questions.s: Which wing's language was recognised along with Urdu as a state language in the 1956 Constitution?
questions.e: Bengali was recognised as a state language with Urdu in 1956, a result of the language movement in East Pakistan. English was an official language.

questions.s: In which year did the Governor-General dissolve the first Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Ghulam Muhammad dissolved it in October 1954, which led to the Tamizuddin Khan case. 1956 was when the first constitution came.

questions.s: Who presided over the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 11 August 1947 after being elected?
questions.e: Jinnah became its first president. Tamizuddin Khan later became its president but not at the first sitting.

questions.s: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
questions.e: The four provinces are Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Islamabad is a capital territory, and Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir are administered separately.

questions.s: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by area?
questions.e: Balochistan covers nearly half of the country's land but has a low population. Punjab has the largest population but a much smaller area.

questions.s: Which is the most populous province of Pakistan?
questions.e: Punjab has the largest number of people. Balochistan is the largest in area, so area and population point to different provinces.

questions.s: Which is the smallest of the four provinces by area?
questions.e: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the smallest by area among the four provinces, even smaller than Sindh. Punjab is larger than both.

questions.s: What is the capital of Balochistan?
questions.e: Quetta, a high-altitude city in the north of the province, is the provincial capital. Gwadar is the well-known port city.

questions.s: What is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
questions.e: Peshawar is the provincial capital and lies near the Khyber Pass. Abbottabad and Mardan are other large cities.

questions.s: What is the capital of Sindh?
questions.e: Karachi is the capital of Sindh and the largest city of Pakistan. Hyderabad was its capital earlier on in history.

questions.s: Which sea lies to the south of Pakistan?
questions.e: Pakistan's coast, with Karachi and Gwadar, is on the Arabian Sea. The Bay of Bengal is east of India.

questions.s: Which country lies to the north-east of Pakistan and shares the Karakoram Highway?
questions.e: China lies in the north-east, and the Karakoram Highway crosses the Khunjerab Pass to join the two countries. Iran is to the south-west.

questions.s: Which neighbour of Pakistan lies to the south-west?
questions.e: Iran borders Balochistan in the south-west. India lies to the east, Afghanistan to the west and north, and China to the north-east.

questions.s: The narrow strip of Afghan land that separates Pakistan from Tajikistan is the
questions.e: The Wakhan Corridor extends to China and keeps Pakistan and Tajikistan apart. The Khyber is a mountain pass, not a corridor between states.

questions.s: Which is the longest river of Pakistan?
questions.e: The Indus flows from the north to the Arabian Sea and is the backbone of Pakistan's agriculture. The others are its tributaries.

questions.s: The Indus River falls into the sea near
questions.e: The Indus forms a delta near Keti Bandar in the Thatta district of Sindh. Gwadar and Ormara lie on the Balochistan coast.

questions.s: The Indus River has its source in
questions.e: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and flows through Ladakh into Pakistan. The Kabul River is the one that comes from Afghanistan.

questions.s: Which of these is a tributary of the Indus on its right bank?
questions.e: The Kabul joins the Indus from the west near Attock. Jhelum, Ravi and Sutlej join on the left, eastern side.

questions.s: The Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi are tributaries of the Indus that come from the
questions.e: These rivers flow from the Himalayan side on the east of the Indus. The Kabul and Gomal join from the west.

questions.s: The Panjnad is formed by the meeting of which rivers?
questions.e: Panjnad means five rivers, formed by the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej. It then joins the Indus near Mithankot.

questions.s: The Panjnad River joins the Indus near
questions.e: After the five rivers meet in southern Punjab, the Panjnad flows to the Indus at Mithankot. Attock is where the Kabul joins the Indus.

questions.s: The Kabul River joins the Indus at
questions.e: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock, in the north of Punjab. Kalabagh and Taunsa lie farther downstream on the Indus.

questions.s: Which river flows through Lahore?
questions.e: The Ravi passes the northern edge of Lahore. The Chenab flows near Multan and Sialkot, and the Jhelum near the city of Jhelum.

questions.s: Which river forms part of the boundary between Sindh and Balochistan near Karachi?
questions.e: The Hub River marks part of the Sindh-Balochistan border west of Karachi. The Kabul and Swat flow in KP and the Zhob in Balochistan.

questions.s: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in
questions.e: India and Pakistan signed it in 1960 with the World Bank. It allotted the three western rivers to Pakistan and the three eastern to India.

questions.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which three rivers were allotted to Pakistan?
questions.e: The western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, were allotted to Pakistan. Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, the eastern ones, went to India.

questions.s: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
questions.e: Tarbela is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world and sits on the Indus in KP. Mangla is on the Jhelum.

questions.s: Mangla Dam is built on which river?
questions.e: Mangla lies on the Jhelum, near Mirpur in Azad Kashmir. Tarbela is on the Indus.

questions.s: Warsak Dam is built on which river?
questions.e: Warsak is on the Kabul River near Peshawar. It provides power and irrigation to the Peshawar valley.

questions.s: Which barrage was opened on the Indus in 1932 and later named after a city in Sindh?
questions.e: The Lloyd, now Sukkur, Barrage came into service in 1932 and irrigates large parts of Sindh. Guddu came in 1962.

questions.s: Which is the highest mountain peak of Pakistan?
questions.e: K2 reaches 8,611 m and is the second highest mountain in the world. Nanga Parbat is lower at about 8,126 m.

questions.s: K2 is located in which mountain range?
questions.e: K2 stands in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan. The Hindu Kush has Tirich Mir.

questions.s: Which peak is known as the 'Killer Mountain'?
questions.e: Nanga Parbat earned the name because many climbers died on it. It is the ninth highest peak in the world.

questions.s: Tirich Mir is the highest peak of which range?
questions.e: Tirich Mir, in Chitral, rises to about 7,700 m and is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush. K2 is in the Karakoram.

questions.s: The highest peak of the Sulaiman Range is
questions.e: Takht-e-Sulaiman is the highest peak of the Sulaiman Range. Sakesar is in the Salt Range and Koh-e-Sufaid is a separate range.

questions.s: Sakesar is the highest peak of the
questions.e: Sakesar, at about 1,500 m, is the highest point of the Salt Range in Punjab. The Margalla Hills overlook Islamabad.

questions.s: The Khewra salt mine lies in which range?
questions.e: Khewra, near Pind Dadan Khan, is one of the largest salt mines in the world. It lies in the Salt Range.

questions.s: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with
questions.e: The Khyber Pass leads from Peshawar to Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan. For centuries invaders came to the subcontinent by it.

questions.s: The Khunjerab Pass lies on the border with
questions.e: At about 4,700 m, Khunjerab is the highest paved border crossing in the world and links Pakistan with China. It is crossed by the Karakoram Highway.

questions.s: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with
questions.e: The Bolan Pass runs through the mountains to link Quetta with the plains near Sibi. Khojak is the pass towards Kandahar.

questions.s: Which pass connects Quetta with Kandahar in Afghanistan?
questions.e: The Khojak Pass crosses the Toba Kakar range to Chaman and then Kandahar. Lowari links Dir with Chitral.

questions.s: The Lowari Pass lies between Dir and
questions.e: The Lowari Pass connects Dir with Chitral in KP. It remains closed by snow in winter, so a tunnel was built there.

questions.s: The Shandur Pass, known for a polo festival, lies between Chitral and
questions.e: Shandur is a high plateau pass between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan, where Chitral and Gilgit teams play polo. It is not near Skardu.

questions.s: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which province?
questions.e: Tharparkar in south-east Sindh is part of the Thar Desert, which extends into India. Cholistan is in Punjab.

questions.s: The Cholistan Desert is found near which city?
questions.e: Cholistan, called Rohi locally, lies in southern Punjab near Bahawalpur. The Thar is in Sindh.

questions.s: Which desert lies in Balochistan?
questions.e: The Kharan Desert is in the Chagai and Kharan area of Balochistan. The Thal is in Punjab between the Indus and Jhelum.

questions.s: Which is the largest city and main seaport of Pakistan?
questions.e: Karachi handles most of the sea trade of the country. Gwadar is a deep-sea port that is newer.

questions.s: Gwadar became part of Pakistan after being obtained from
questions.e: Pakistan purchased Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958. It had never been part of British India.

questions.s: Which lake in Sindh is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan?
questions.e: Manchar Lake, in Dadu district, is the largest freshwater lake. Keenjhar supplies water to Karachi and is smaller.

questions.s: Lake Saiful Muluk is a lake in which valley?
questions.e: Saiful Muluk lies near Naran at the head of the Kaghan Valley in KP. The Neelum Valley is in Azad Kashmir.

questions.s: The Deosai Plains are a high plateau in
questions.e: Deosai lies near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan and is a national park known for its brown bears. It is not in the lowland provinces.

questions.s: The Baltoro Glacier lies in which range?
questions.e: The Baltoro Glacier flows near K2 in the Karakoram. It is one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

questions.s: Which valley is called the 'Switzerland of the East' in Pakistan?
questions.e: Swat, in KP, is often given this name for its green hills and rivers. Hunza is famous for its mountain views and is in Gilgit-Baltistan.

questions.s: The Potohar Plateau lies between which two rivers?
questions.e: The Potohar Plateau lies between the Indus and the Jhelum, around Rawalpindi and Islamabad. It is mostly rain-fed.

questions.s: Islamabad lies at the foot of which hills?
questions.e: The capital lies below the Margalla Hills in the Potohar region. The Salt Range is farther south in Punjab.

questions.s: What is the national language of Pakistan?
questions.e: Urdu is the national language and links people of all provinces. Punjabi, Sindhi and Pashto are widely spoken regional languages.

questions.s: Which is the most widely spoken first language in Pakistan?
questions.e: Punjabi is the mother tongue of the largest share of people, though Urdu is the national language and understood almost everywhere.

questions.s: Which colour on the national flag of Pakistan represents the Muslim majority?
questions.e: The dark green field stands for the Muslim majority, and the white stripe for minorities. The crescent stands for progress and the star for light and knowledge.

questions.s: The white vertical stripe on the national flag represents
questions.e: The white band stands for the non-Muslim citizens of the country. The green field represents the majority.

questions.s: Who wrote the lyrics of the national anthem of Pakistan?
questions.e: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the words, and the tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla. Iqbal is the national poet but did not write the anthem.

questions.s: Who is regarded as the national poet of Pakistan?
questions.e: Allama Iqbal is called the national poet and the thinker of Pakistan. Ghalib lived and wrote in Delhi in the nineteenth century.

questions.s: The national animal of Pakistan is the
questions.e: The markhor, a wild goat with spiral horns, is the national animal. The snow leopard and the Indus dolphin are other important wildlife species of the country.

questions.s: The national flower of Pakistan is
questions.e: The jasmine, locally called chambeli, is the national flower. The rose and tulip are not national symbols of Pakistan.

questions.s: The national tree of Pakistan is the
questions.e: The deodar, a tall cedar of the northern mountains, is the national tree. The chinar is associated with Kashmir.

questions.s: The national bird of Pakistan is the
questions.e: The chukar partridge is the national bird. The peacock is the national bird of the neighbouring country, India.

questions.s: The national fruit of Pakistan is the
questions.e: The mango, the 'king of fruits', is the national fruit, and Pakistan is a major producer. Apples are grown mostly in the cooler north.

questions.s: The national game of Pakistan is
questions.e: Field hockey is officially the national game, although cricket is more widely followed. Pakistan won Olympic gold in hockey three times.

questions.s: The motto of Pakistan is
questions.e: The national motto, Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem, was given by Quaid-e-Azam. The other options are not Pakistan's motto.

questions.s: The four crops shown on the national emblem of Pakistan include cotton, jute, tea and
questions.e: The wreath on the emblem shows cotton, jute, tea and wheat, the main crops at independence. Rice and sugarcane are not shown.

questions.s: The Central Bank of Pakistan is the
questions.e: The State Bank of Pakistan was set up in 1948 and Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated it. The other banks are commercial banks.

questions.s: Mohenjo-daro is located in which province?
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro lies near Larkana in Sindh on the banks of the Indus. Harappa lies in Punjab.

questions.s: Harappa is located in which province?
questions.e: Harappa lies in Punjab, near the old course of the Ravi. Mohenjo-daro is in Sindh.

questions.s: The ruins of Mohenjo-daro belong to which ancient civilisation?
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro was a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, about 4,500 years old. Gandhara is associated with Taxila and Peshawar.

questions.s: Which famous structure was found at Mohenjo-daro?
questions.e: The Great Bath was a large public pool of fired brick. The city also had a good drainage system.

questions.s: Taxila was a centre of which ancient civilisation?
questions.e: Taxila was a centre of Gandhara learning and Buddhist art and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site. Mughal rule came much later.

questions.s: In which year were Mohenjo-daro, Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi first inscribed as UNESCO sites?
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro, Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi were inscribed in 1980. Lahore Fort and the Shalimar Gardens followed in 1981.

questions.s: Lahore Fort and the Shalimar Gardens are on the UNESCO list from the year
questions.e: The two Lahore sites were inscribed together in 1981. Rohtas Fort joined the list in 1997.

questions.s: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum was built by
questions.e: Sher Shah Suri raised Rohtas in the sixteenth century to keep control of the Gakhar region. The other three were Mughals who ruled afterwards.

questions.s: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built by
questions.e: Aurangzeb Alamgir built it in 1673. Jahangir is buried in Lahore at Shahdara, and Shah Jahan built the Shalimar Gardens.

questions.s: Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were built by the emperor
questions.e: Shah Jahan had the garden laid out in the 1640s. Aurangzeb is remembered for the Badshahi Mosque.

questions.s: Faisal Mosque in Islamabad was designed by a
questions.e: Vedat Dalokay of Turkey designed it, in the shape of a Bedouin tent. It was funded by Saudi Arabia and named after King Faisal.

questions.s: Which UNESCO site is a Buddhist monastery in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
questions.e: Takht-i-Bahi, near Mardan, is a Buddhist monastic complex of the early centuries AD. Rohtas is a fort and Makli is a necropolis.

questions.s: The oldest Neolithic farming site in Pakistan, near the Bolan Pass, is
questions.e: Mehrgarh, in Balochistan, shows early farming from about 7000 BC. Harappa belongs to the later Indus cities.

questions.s: Which city is known as the 'Manchester of Pakistan' because of its textile industry?
questions.e: Faisalabad is the centre of cotton and textile mills. Lahore is better known for gardens and culture.

questions.s: Which city of Punjab is famous for its sports goods and surgical instruments?
questions.e: Sialkot exports footballs, sports goods and surgical tools. Sargodha is better known for citrus.

questions.s: Which city is famous for citrus fruit, especially the kinnow?
questions.e: Sargodha district is Pakistan's chief citrus-growing area. Sukkur is on the Indus and known for its barrage.

questions.s: Which is the main cash crop of Pakistan?
questions.e: Cotton is the main cash crop, widely grown in Punjab and Sindh and the basis of the textile industry. Wheat is the staple food crop.

questions.s: Which crop is the staple food grain of Pakistan?
questions.e: Wheat is the major grain sown in the rabi season and eaten as roti. Cotton and tobacco are cash crops.

questions.s: Which of these is a rabi crop?
questions.e: Rabi crops are sown in autumn and harvested in spring, and wheat is the chief one. Rice, cotton and maize are kharif crops.

questions.s: Which of these is a kharif crop?
questions.e: Kharif crops are sown with the summer monsoon and rice is the best known. Wheat, gram and barley are rabi crops.

questions.s: Natural gas was discovered in Pakistan at
questions.e: Gas was found at Sui in Balochistan in 1952. Thar is known for coal, and Khewra for salt.

questions.s: The large lignite coal reserves of Pakistan are in
questions.e: The Thar desert in Sindh holds one of the largest lignite deposits in the world. Swat and Hunza are in the north.

questions.s: Which Balochistan district holds the Saindak copper-gold project?
questions.e: Saindak lies in Chagai district, near the Iranian border. Gwadar and Kech are on the coast.

questions.s: Which mineral is mined in large amounts at Khewra?
questions.e: Khewra is one of the largest salt mines in the world. Coal is found in the Thar and Salt Range, but this is not Khewra's main product.

questions.s: Which language of Balochistan belongs to the Dravidian family?
questions.e: Brahui is a Dravidian language spoken in Balochistan, an unusual situation among Iranian languages. Balochi, Pashto and Persian are Indo-Iranian.

questions.s: The Kalash people live in the valleys of which district?
questions.e: The Kalash live in Bumburet, Birir and Rumbur valleys in Chitral and have a distinct culture and festivals. Swat is a separate district.

questions.s: Which poet is known for the Sindhi collection Shah Jo Risalo?
questions.e: Shah Abdul Latif of Bhit Shah composed the Risalo in Sindhi. Bulleh Shah wrote in Punjabi and Rahman Baba in Pashto.
